UnitStatement: DeclarationsEditor is the rule-pack declarations editor (Phase C2 slice 4, TP-C2-DECLEDITOR-001) providing structured form controls for declaring a rule pack's inputs and value slots.
PRD §14.5 requires the rule-pack editor to let a user declare the rule pack's inputs and user-supplied value slots — the named variables a formula's variable_ref binds to.
The declarations editor boundary is purely structured form controls with no writable expression text syntax (D-02b AWAITING_RULING).

The unknown-dimension and unknown-slot-kind placeholder is the uppercase "TBD" token the codec and schema accept (CONTRACT no-silent-defaults); placeholders are private-by-default with no silent defaults.

A patched declaration entry keeps every member it already carried (provenance, const-true relaxation flags, missing-value diagnostic) and untouched sibling entries round-trip verbatim — lossless editing.

UserSuppliedValueSlot carries a dimension/unit intent and a value_status, not a number; the actual private allowable value is not an authored member of this schema version, so the honest value_status marker is exposed instead of inventing a value field.

A required input whose source_kind is private_library_value additionally authors a library_value_ref (library_kind / library_id / record_id / slot_id) — the pointer the C4 rule-check runner resolves from the local private-library store at run time (TP-C3-LIBREFAUTHOR-001).
The library reference is carried but the private value is NEVER embedded in the rule-pack document (IP boundary, PRD §13/§17.3), so authoring a reference never redistributes a private value.

A required input whose source_kind is solver_result additionally authors a solver_result_ref (a single result_id) — the pointer the C4 rule-check runner resolves from the solved result envelope's results[] by id at run time (TP-C4-SOLVERREFAUTHOR-001).

The solver_result_ref is the in-pack canonical form of the previously caller-supplied {input_id, result_id} solver binding (PRD §12.5); an authored reference governs its input alone and supersedes the run panel's per-input result selector.
An unfilled or unresolvable reference leaves the input unsupplied so the check blocks at RULE_INPUTS_INCOMPLETE — never a silent pass.
library_value_ref (DEC-038) and solver_result_ref (DEC-039) are ratified schema members, carried at rule-pack schema_version 0.4.0.

Declaration quantity_intent unit refs use the reviewed DEC-018 catalog when the desktop backend exposes it; browser preview and backend-unavailable routes keep prior text input rather than synthesizing unit options (TP-UNITS-B2-RULEPACKUNITS-001).
The unit picker filters catalog entries by the selected dimension, keeps any stored out-of-catalog value visible as the current value, and never silently rewrites a dimension/unit pair.

SOURCE_KINDS enum vocabulary: solver_result, model_input, user_supplied_rule_value, private_library_value, owner_design_basis, TBD — copied verbatim from rule_pack.schema.yaml so controls only emit schema-valid tokens.
REQUIRED_FOR_TARGETS enum vocabulary: rule_check, reporting, diagnostic, TBD.
COMPLETENESS_STATUSES enum vocabulary: complete, missing_required_value, missing_unit, missing_provenance, missing_redistribution_status, review_pending, TBD.
SLOT_KINDS enum vocabulary: allowable, stress_limit, ratio_limit, coefficient, category_threshold, source_reference, TBD.
VALUE_STATUSES enum vocabulary: not_provided, private_user_supplied, public_permissive_reviewed, invented_non_engineering_example, protected_suspected, TBD.

LIBRARY_KINDS vocabulary is material, section, component — copied verbatim from rule_pack.schema.yaml; it has NO TBD member, so a seeded reference defaults library_kind to the first kind and leaves the ids as visible TBD placeholders.
uniqueDeclarationId(prefix, existingIds) generates a unique declaration id of the form <prefix>_<n>, skipping any id already present, matching the schema Id pattern.
readRequiredInputIds(document) returns the declared input_ids in document order (empty when none or malformed).
readValueSlotIds(document) returns the declared slot_ids in document order (empty when none or malformed).

defaultRequiredInput(existingIds) returns a schema-valid private placeholder RequiredInput with a fresh unique id, uppercase TBD dimension placeholder, const-true relaxation flags emitted true, and no invented value.

A default required input is seeded with source_kind user_supplied_rule_value, required_for rule_check, completeness_status missing_required_value, missing_value_diagnostic RULE_INPUT_MISSING, and redistribution_status private_only.
defaultValueSlot(existingIds) returns a schema-valid private placeholder UserSuppliedValueSlot with a fresh unique id, TBD slot kind/dimension, and not_provided value status (no value invented).

defaultLibraryValueRef() returns a schema-valid LibraryValueRef with all four members: library_kind defaulting to the first kind (material), and library_id/record_id/slot_id as visible uppercase TBD placeholders so an unfilled reference resolves to nothing and the input blocks.

defaultSolverResultRef() returns a schema-shaped SolverResultRef carrying the single required result_id member as the visible uppercase TBD placeholder; an unfilled reference matches no result row so the input blocks (never a silent pass).
setRequiredInputs(document, inputs) returns a new document with the required_inputs array replaced.
setValueSlots(document, slots) returns a new document with the value_slots array replaced.
hasTauriInternals() returns whether window.__TAURI_INTERNALS__ is present, used to detect the desktop runtime versus browser preview.

unitOptions(route, dimensionId, currentSymbol) builds the unit option list filtered by dimension from the tauri_unit_catalog route, sorting canonical units first, and prepends the current/fallback symbol when absent.

UnitRefField preserves the previous free-text behavior until the desktop catalog is available so browser preview does not invent a fallback catalog; with the catalog it renders a dimension-filtered select.
EnumSelect surfaces a stored token outside the current vocabulary as a "(current)" option rather than silently snapping it to a default, so the user sees exactly what is stored.
DeclarationsEditor patches one required input by index while untouched entries round-trip verbatim (updateInput).

changeInputSourceKind: switching to private_library_value seeds a placeholder library_value_ref when none exists, and switching to solver_result seeds a placeholder solver_result_ref, so the sub-form opens with a complete schema-valid (unresolved, blocking) reference.

Switching a required input's source_kind away from a reference kind leaves any existing reference in place (lossless); its sub-form stays visible so a now-meaningless reference is never silently hidden, and an explicit Remove control lets the user drop it.

updateInputLibraryRef merges a patch into the existing library_value_ref (or a fresh default when none exists) so the first field edit always produces a complete four-member reference, never a schema-invalid partial.
removeInputLibraryRef drops the library_value_ref member entirely — the only member-removing edit the editor exposes — while every other member of the input round-trips verbatim.
removeInputSolverRef drops the solver_result_ref member entirely, returning the input to the run-panel caller-supplied binding path, with every other member round-tripping verbatim.
Removing a required input is blocked when only one remains, with the stated reason "A rule pack needs at least one required input."
Removing a value slot is blocked when only one remains, with the stated reason "A rule pack needs at least one value slot."

The private-library reference sub-form is shown whenever the input draws from a private library OR whenever a reference is already present, so a reference left over from a since-changed source_kind stays visible and removable rather than silently hidden.
The referenced private-library value is resolved at check-run time from the local private library store; it stays in the library and is never embedded in the rule pack.

A solver-result reference binds the input to a specific row of the solved result envelope by result id, resolved at check-run time; an authored reference is the canonical binding that supersedes the run panel's per-input result selector.

ExpressionComposer.test.tsx (TP-C2-COMPOSER-001) tests the structured AST expression composer; pure-helper tests pin grammar v1.0.0 node encoding and the lossless document rewrite, component tests drive visible controls.
collectRulePackVariables collects declared required-input and value-slot variables, yielding ids user_required_input_1 (required_input) and user_limit_slot_1 (value_slot) for the draft document.

The schema's ExpressionQuantity is additionalProperties:false and allows only value/dimension/unit_ref; the unit_required/dimension_check_required relaxation flags are not authorable in pack documents (absent means true).
The unknown-dimension placeholder is the uppercase "TBD" token the codec (decode_quantity) and schema DimensionId accept — never lowercase "tbd".
defaultExpressionNode("literal") equals {node:literal, quantity:{value:0, dimension:TBD, unit_ref:TBD}}.
A default table node carries two strictly-increasing rows so interpolate is immediately well-formed, with TBD placeholders; a lookup node additionally carries an exact mode.

The dimension vocabulary offers only the codec/schema tokens with the uppercase TBD placeholder; a lowercase "tbd" default (the slice-2 regression) produced documents that fail backend decode and DimensionId schema validation.
Table nodes (interpolate, lookup) are editable as of slice 3; refusal markers and unknown tags remain non-editable and are preserved read-only.
setFormulaExpression rewrites one formula's expression AST while preserving the untouched sibling formula and the payload's other members (e.g. payload_kind).
parseRulePackDocument reports failure honestly: null text yields no-draft, invalid JSON and a top-level array are rejected, and a valid object yields {ok:true, document}.
renderExpressionText renders a read-only AST text preview without changing canonical AST shape, e.g. a compare/divide tree renders as "((stress_actual / 2 1 [dimensionless]) <= stress_limit)".
renderExpressionText renders unsafe_host_access as "[refusal:unsafe_host_access]" and an unrecognized node as "[unrecognized:future_feature]".
Adding a table row appends with strict monotonicity (last argument + 1); the last row cannot be removed because the schema requires at least one row.
Editing a table node's argument expression preserves the table metadata and rows verbatim — only the argument subtree changes.
An unrecognized node renders read-only with an honest explanation and survives intact when an editable sibling is edited (not dropped or rewritten).
Refusal-marker nodes (unsupported_form / unsafe_host_access) are always read-only, expose no node-type selector so they cannot be silently switched, and round-trip byte-for-byte.

ExpressionComposer is the structured AST expression composer (Phase C2 slice 2, TP-C2-COMPOSER-001), a recursive form/tree composer that builds the frozen grammar v1.0.0 typed AST (DEC-022) so a user never writes node-tagged JSON by hand.
PRD §14.5 requires the rule-pack editor to provide an Expression editor.

The composer boundary (D-02b RULED, DEC-037) is purely structured: it may show a labeled read-only one-way AST-to-text preview but provides no writable expression text input and no parser; the typed AST remains the sole canonical checksum-bound form (DEC-022).

Table-backed nodes (interpolate / lookup) are authored through a structured table sub-editor (TP-C2-TABLENODE-001): table id, argument/result dimension and unit refs, the {argument, result} rows, plus the recursive argument expression.
Monotonicity and out-of-range remain evaluator-enforced diagnostics surfaced as authoring guidance, never silently clamped in the composer.

Expression literal/table unit refs use the reviewed DEC-018 catalog when the desktop backend exposes it; browser preview keeps manual unit text and stored out-of-catalog units remain visible and selectable (TP-UNITS-B2-RULEEXPRUNITS-001).

Any unrecognized node tag and the refusal markers (unsupported_form / unsafe_host_access) are rendered read-only and preserved verbatim; the composer never silently drops or rewrites a subtree it does not edit.

EDITABLE_NODE_TYPES is the full frozen grammar v1.0.0 set: literal, variable_ref, unary, binary, compare, logical, select, aggregate, interpolate, lookup; refusal markers and unrecognized tags are excluded.
UNARY_OPERATORS are negate, abs, not.
BINARY_OPERATORS are add, subtract, multiply, divide.
COMPARE_OPERATORS are less_than, less_than_or_equal, greater_than, greater_than_or_equal, equal, not_equal.
LOGICAL_OPERATORS are and, or.
AGGREGATE_FUNCTIONS are min, max.
LOOKUP_MODES are exact, step.

The DIMENSIONS vocabulary matches the document codec and schema (core/rules/rule_pack_document DIMENSION_TOKENS == schema DimensionId == evaluator Dimension enum), with uppercase TBD as the honest unknown-dimension authoring default.

DIMENSIONS enumerates dimensionless, length, mass, time, temperature, temperature_interval, angle, rotation, force, moment, pressure, stress, area, volume, density, linear_stiffness, rotational_stiffness, displacement, velocity, acceleration, thermal_conductivity, specific_heat, thermal_expansion_coefficient, second_moment_area, section_modulus, mass_per_length, volume_per_length, slope, TBD.
FormulaDeclaration carries index, id, kind, and the expression AST node.
parseRulePackDocument parses draft document text into an object, honestly reporting failure as no-draft, invalid-json, or not-an-object.

collectRulePackVariables collects the variable identifiers a variable_ref may bind — declared required inputs and value slots; solver-result fields are bound at evaluation time, not invented into the picker.
readFormulaDeclarations reads the formula declarations and their expression ASTs, defaulting a missing expression to {node:unrecognized} and formula_kind to derived_quantity.
setFormulaExpression returns a new document with formulaId's expression AST replaced, preserving every other member and every other formula by structural copy.
nodeKind returns the declared node tag of an AST node, or "unrecognized" when absent.
isEditableNode returns whether a node's kind is in EDITABLE_NODE_TYPES.
isTableNode returns whether a node is an interpolate or lookup node.
defaultLiteral returns {node:literal, quantity:{value:0, dimension:TBD, unit_ref:TBD}}; the relaxation flags are omitted because the codec/evaluator treat absent flags as true (strict).

defaultUserTable returns a schema-valid table with two strictly-increasing rows so an interpolate node is immediately well-formed (evaluator requires at least two rows and strict monotonicity), with TBD dimension/unit placeholders.
defaultExpressionNode(type, variables) returns a sensible default node of the given editable type used when creating or switching nodes.

renderExpressionText provides deterministic read-only rendering for DEC-037's permitted one-way AST text preview; it is display-only, no parser consumes the string, and the AST remains the canonical checksummed member.

DimensionSelect is a shared dimension picker over the codec/schema vocabulary, reused by the literal editor and both table dimension fields, and exported so the declarations editor draws from the same single vocabulary.

DimensionSelect performs no silent display-snap: a stored token outside the current vocabulary surfaces as a "(current)" option rather than being shown as TBD while the document still holds the real token (CONTRACT no-silent-defaults).
ExpressionNodeEditor renders refusal markers and unrecognized node tags read-only with the subtree round-tripping unchanged; table-backed nodes are editable.
The table sub-editor patches only the touched row while every other row object round-trips verbatim (updateRow).
addRow appends a new row with argument equal to the last argument + 1 (or 0 when empty) to preserve strict monotonicity.
Table guidance states row arguments must be strictly increasing, interpolate needs at least two rows, and the evaluator blocks out-of-range arguments — it never extrapolates or clamps.
An aggregate node defaults its function to min and blocks removing its last operand with the reason "An aggregate needs at least one operand."

ExpressionComposer renders the full composer surface: a variable browser, a formula selector, and the recursive node editor for the selected formula's expression AST; the parent owns serialization and persistence.

RulePackManagerPanel.test.tsx (Phase C2 slice 1, TP-C2-EDITOR-001) pins the honest browser-preview seam: jsdom has no Tauri runtime, so drafts stay in memory and every backend action reports the explicit desktop-only diagnostic instead of a synthesized fallback.
RulePackManagerPanel scopes the manager to the loaded project, showing "create or open a local project first" without one and the project id plus "local SQLite only" with one.

A new draft is private-by-default: rule_pack_kind open_pipe_stress_rule_pack, grammar_version 1.0.0, classification privacy_class private_user_data and redistribution_status private_only; discard clears the draft.
In browser preview, validate and refresh-list backend actions report the explicit RULE-PACK-BACKEND-DESKTOP-ONLY diagnostic.
Compute-checksum and save route to the desktop-only seam (RULE-PACK-BACKEND-DESKTOP-ONLY) from a clean draft state in browser preview.
Save is blocked with the honest reason "create or open a local project first" when no project is loaded.
Invalid draft JSON is reported honestly as RULE-PACK-DRAFT-JSON-INVALID instead of being acted upon.
The boundary note keeps the DEC-037 and professional boundaries visible: read-only, no expression text parser, never committed to the repository, never a code-compliance claim.
The structured composer is revealed only with a draft, and a structured edit (switching the formula's root node to compare) rewrites the canonical document JSON the validate/save flow reads.

The declarations editor and expression composer read the same draft document (slice 4, TP-C2-DECLEDITOR-001), so a required input added through the editor is immediately bindable in the composer's variable picker — no raw JSON.
The check-definitions editor (slice 5, TP-C2-CHECKDEF-001) reads the same draft document; adding a check grows the canonical document JSON.
A freshly declared required input is immediately bindable in a check's reference picker, since the declarations editor and check editor read the same draft.

buildDraftRulePackDocument builds a schema-shaped private draft with schema_version 0.4.0, grammar_version 1.0.0, payload grammar_status frozen_open_pipe_stress_declared_expression, and a variable_ref root expression.
The draft professional_boundary sets software_makes_compliance_claim false and human_review_required true.

stampChecksumIntoDocument stamps a computed checksum (sha256, JCS canonicalization, payload_scope rule_pack_payload, basis rfc8785_jcs_sha256_excluding_checksums) into checksums.rule_pack_checksum with verification_status verified, without touching other members.
